overview: Create shared symbols, input-validation helpers, safe serialization and the embedded scientific figure style. These utilities keep the symbolic calculation separate from numerical substitution and make the actual font and export settings inspectable.
workflow: Import algebra, numerical, plotting, notebook-display and export utilities.
Declare the real scan angle and general complex tensor coefficients.
Define conversions that reject invalid inputs without evaluating arbitrary text.
Load the supplied scientific style and record the font actually available.

blocks.title: Import the common infrastructure
blocks.explanation: SymPy stores exact matrices and expressions; NumPy evaluates numerical arrays; pyplot creates figures. base64, csv, io, json and zipfile support downloadable data. copy protects saved configurations from later edits, html escapes displayed labels and traceback records diagnostic errors. contextmanager supports input transactions and lru_cache avoids recomputing fixed symbolic source algebra. The IPython display objects render notebook text and mathematics.
blocks.why: The calculation, reports and downloads must share numerical conventions rather than redefine slightly different helper functions in different workflows.
blocks.check: Importing these modules should succeed after Cell 1. Notebook display imports are a presentation dependency; a browser adapter may replace only that presentation layer.

blocks.title: Declare symbols and provisional display defaults
blocks.explanation: sp.init_printing prepares symbolic display. The initial rcParams values are provisional and are superseded by apply_scientific_style at the end of this cell. α is explicitly real because it is an angle. The six coefficients a through f are explicitly complex so conjugation and relative phases remain available in every tensor calculation.
blocks.why: Declaring all tensor coefficients real would erase phase-sensitive interference. The analyzer scan α must also remain separate from the frame angle ψ introduced by the orientation inputs.
blocks.check: sp.conjugate(α) simplifies to α, while sp.conjugate(a) remains a distinct conjugate symbol. The final style font size is 22, not the provisional value 10.

blocks.title: real_number: require a finite real scalar
blocks.explanation: The function numerically evaluates its input with sp.N, attempts conversion to a complex scalar and rejects unresolved expressions. It then rejects NaN, infinity or an imaginary part larger than the stated numerical tolerance. The returned value is the real part as a Python floating-point number.
blocks.why: Lattice lengths, angles, magnitudes and integer-rule controls cannot be unresolved symbolic expressions or complex-valued numbers.
blocks.check: A finite value such as 1.25 is accepted. An unresolved symbol, infinity or a value such as 1+0.1j raises a named input error.

blocks.title: exact: retain an entered decimal as a rational
blocks.explanation: First call real_number to validate the scalar. Then construct sp.Rational from the decimal string of the numerical value. A typical entered decimal 0.8 therefore becomes the exact rational 4/5 for later symbolic operations.
blocks.why: Exact rational coefficients make cancellations and printed derivations easier to inspect and reduce unnecessary floating-point residues in otherwise exact example cases.
blocks.check: exact(0.8) should equal sp.Rational(4,5). This preserves the validated numerical decimal; it does not recover an arbitrary symbolic expression that was already rounded before entry.

blocks.title: deg: convert degrees to radians
blocks.explanation: SymPy trigonometric functions use radians. Multiplication by π/180 converts a user-facing degree value while retaining exact forms for special angles such as 45 degrees.
blocks.why: Mixing degree-valued UI controls with radian-valued sine and cosine would silently produce incorrect orientations and polarization vectors.
blocks.check: deg(90) equals π/2 and sin(deg(30)) equals 1/2.

blocks.title: numeric: evaluate a symbolic matrix
blocks.explanation: Convert the input to a SymPy matrix, evaluate its resolved entries and construct a NumPy array with complex dtype. The complex dtype is retained even when some entries happen to be real.
blocks.why: Numerical amplitudes and Jones states can contain complex entries. Converting them to a real array would discard physical phases.
blocks.check: numeric(Matrix([1,I])) must retain the second entry as 1j. All free symbols must be substituted before this conversion is used for a final result.

blocks.title: zero: test an exact symbolic identity
blocks.explanation: Every entry is expanded and simplified, and all entries must equal symbolic zero. Scalar identities can be supplied as a one-entry matrix, while matrix identities are tested entry by entry.
blocks.why: Algebraic regressions should test a mathematical identity directly instead of accepting two sampled curves that only look similar.
blocks.check: zero(T.T*T-eye(3)) is an appropriate exact check for an exact frame. A numerical approximate frame is instead checked with tolerance by validate_frame.

blocks.title: tidy: perform local algebraic simplification
blocks.explanation: For a matrix, apply the same function to each entry. For a scalar, expand multiplication and factor common terms. The helper intentionally avoids a broad global trigonometric search.
blocks.why: The reports need readable formulas, but repeated expensive global simplification can make general complex-tensor calculations unnecessarily slow.
blocks.check: The tidied expression must remain algebraically equal to its input; this operation never fits coefficients or shifts a polar curve.

blocks.title: complex_parameter: construct magnitude and phase
blocks.explanation: Validate the coefficient magnitude and phase as real finite numbers, reject a negative magnitude and form ρ*exp(I*φ*π/180). Both entered numbers pass through exact before building the symbolic coefficient.
blocks.why: The magnitude/phase UI corresponds directly to the physical parameterization q=|q|exp(i arg(q)); a relative phase affects complete-mode interference.
blocks.check: A magnitude of 1 and phase of 90 degrees give I. A magnitude of zero gives a zero coefficient independently of phase.

blocks.title: parse_complex: parse custom tensor entries safely
blocks.explanation: Interpret a numerical string with Python complex(), accepting j notation and replacing a literal I with j. Reject non-finite entries, then rebuild the real and imaginary decimal parts as SymPy rational numbers.
blocks.why: Custom tensor text must be numerical data, not executable Python. The function does not call eval or infer a symmetry constraint for the entered tensor.
blocks.check: An entry such as '1+0.2j' is accepted. A Python command or an unresolved expression is rejected. Fractions should be entered as numerical decimals in this parser.

blocks.title: serializable: make result data JSON-compatible
blocks.explanation: The function recursively traverses dictionaries, sequences and arrays. Matrices become rows of string entries, SymPy expressions become strings and NumPy scalars become ordinary Python values. A numerical complex scalar becomes an object with explicitly named real and imaginary parts.
blocks.why: Standard JSON cannot directly store SymPy matrices, arbitrary NumPy objects or complex numbers. Exporting them explicitly prevents silent loss of phase or matrix structure.
blocks.check: A complex coefficient must retain both real and imaginary values in its JSON representation. A symbolic expression is an algebraic record, not an executable instruction on re-import.

blocks.title: check: keep validation active in optimized Python
blocks.explanation: If a condition is false, explicitly raise AssertionError with the supplied explanation. Unlike a bare assert statement, this function is not removed by the Python -O optimization switch.
blocks.why: Scientific consistency checks should not disappear because the interpreter was launched in an optimized mode.
blocks.check: check(False,'test message') raises AssertionError with that message.

blocks.title: Embed the supplied scientific style
blocks.explanation: The style text defines a 6.5-by-5-inch default figure, requested Arial font, a 22-point base font, regular mathematical text, two-point axes and lines, the supplied color cycle and inward ticks. It also defines legend formatting, transparent output, tight bounding boxes, PDF as the default format and 600-dpi saved rasterization.
blocks.why: The notebook must carry the formatting instructions with it so exporting a figure does not depend on a stylesheet that exists only on one computer. Formatting parameters change presentation, not intensity values.
blocks.check: Every result ZIP includes the same sci.mplstyle. PDF/SVG curve geometry remains vector-based; the dpi setting chiefly controls PNG and any rasterized content.

blocks.title: Write and load the embedded style
blocks.explanation: apply_scientific_style obtains a temporary folder, creates it if needed, writes the exact embedded style text as UTF-8 and loads that path with plt.style.use. The function is defined here; it is actually executed by the assignment at the end of the cell.
blocks.why: Using the documented Matplotlib style-sheet mechanism makes the visible configuration reproducible without hard-coding every style parameter separately in every plotting routine.
blocks.check: The temporary sci.mplstyle should exist and the loaded font.size should be 22. The working directory does not need to contain a separate stylesheet.

blocks.title: Choose an installed font and distinguish display from export
blocks.explanation: Try Arial first, then Liberation Sans and DejaVu Sans, with silent font substitution disabled during each lookup. Record the first available font or raise an error if none is found. Set notebook raster display to 110 dpi independently of the 600-dpi export setting; request embedded TrueType PDF/PS fonts and editable SVG text.
blocks.why: A requested font is not necessarily installed. The program should report a real fallback rather than claim an exact Arial match, and screen previews need not be as large as publication PNGs.
blocks.check: PLOT_STYLE_STATUS.actual_font and font_fallback must describe the local environment. Installing Arial allows it to be chosen on the next clean initialization.

blocks.title: Return and retain style provenance
blocks.explanation: Return requested and actual fonts, fallback status, resolved font path, stylesheet path, export resolution and the documentation URL. PLOT_STYLE_STATUS=apply_scientific_style() executes the function once during cell execution and makes this provenance available to later reports and exports.
blocks.why: A shared scientific figure must be auditable: its stated font, dimensions and export settings should describe the settings actually used.
blocks.check: Later result exports should carry plot_style_status.json with this information. None of these paths is a material or tensor input.

blocks.title: Print mathematical symbols
blocks.explanation: raman_latex keeps internal variable names unchanged and prints beta_prime as β′ in equations.
blocks.why: The same symbol should appear in the controls, equations and exported documents.
blocks.check: A symbolic beta_prime must print as β′; numerical expressions remain unchanged.

blocks.title: Confirm that this cell finished executing
blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.
blocks.check: Run Cells 1–2 in order and confirm the Cell 02/22 message. Model/source checks must be inspected separately in Validation.

pitfalls: The initial rcParams font size 10 is overwritten by the supplied style before plotting.
exact() preserves entered decimal numbers as rationals; custom tensor parsing accepts numerical strings rather than arbitrary SymPy formulas.
Arial fallback changes typography, not the calculated polar pattern.
The complex coefficients belong to a phonon tensor. Their phases should not be confused with the optical Jones phase β.

overview: Construct a proper three-dimensional measurement frame from the lattice metric, surface indices and in-plane reference. This is where the crystal-orientation rotation is defined. The column convention is v_crystal=T*v_lab, so a Cartesian Raman tensor transforms as R_lab=T.T*R_crystal*T.
workflow: Build the direct-lattice Cartesian matrix L.
Calculate the reciprocal surface normal L^(-T)*(h,k,l).
Build a normalized in-plane X reference and Y=Z cross X.
Apply the independent frame angle ψ and verify orthonormality and determinant +1.

blocks.title: trig_deg: exact special angles and numerical general angles
blocks.explanation: Convert the degree input to radians with deg(). Compute sine and cosine symbolically. If unresolved trigonometric functions remain, evaluate them to 15 digits; otherwise retain exact radicals such as sqrt(2)/2.
blocks.why: Standard reference planes benefit from exact symbolic matrices, while a general measured miscut angle should still be numerically usable.
blocks.check: 45 degrees retains exact radicals. An arbitrary finite angle yields finite sine/cosine values that satisfy the expected normalization to numerical tolerance.

blocks.title: lattice_matrix: validate six cell parameters
blocks.explanation: Read the three lattice lengths and the three interaxial angles. Require six inputs, positive finite lengths and angles strictly between 0 and 180 degrees. Evaluate the angle cosines and the sine of γ.
blocks.why: The surface normal depends on the lattice metric. Invalid lengths or collapsed angles cannot define a physically usable reciprocal cell.
blocks.check: A cubic unit cell gives lengths (1,1,1) and angles (90,90,90). An angle of zero or a negative length raises a useful error.

blocks.title: lattice_matrix: derive the Cartesian lattice columns
blocks.explanation: Set the first direct vector along Cartesian x and the second in the xy plane. The scaled third-vector y component is (cos(α)-cos(β)*cos(γ))/sin(γ); its z component follows from unit norm. Reject a nonpositive volume factor, then assemble L with the three direct vectors as columns.
blocks.why: Miller indices and direction indices refer to a crystallographic lattice, whereas the tensor acts in orthonormal Cartesian coordinates. L bridges those coordinate descriptions, including skew cells.
blocks.check: For orthorhombic inputs, L is diag(a0,b0,c0). For a valid hexagonal setting, the second lattice vector contains the expected cos(120 degrees) and sin(120 degrees).

blocks.title: real_vector: validate a nonzero three-vector
blocks.explanation: Convert the supplied values to a 3-by-1 SymPy matrix, check the shape and validate every entry as a finite real scalar. Reject a vector whose numerical norm is effectively zero.
blocks.why: A zero surface normal or in-plane direction cannot be normalized. Rejecting it here prevents a later division by zero from being mistaken for a Raman selection-rule result.
blocks.check: [0,1,-1] is valid. [0,0,0] and a vector with the wrong number of entries are rejected.

blocks.title: unit: normalize in Cartesian space
blocks.explanation: Divide a real Cartesian column vector by sqrt(v.T*v), simplifying the result. The transpose is appropriate here because the geometry vectors have already been required to be real.
blocks.why: Direction cosines in an orientation matrix require normalized axes. Applying a Euclidean norm directly to raw skew-cell indices would use the wrong metric.
blocks.check: The returned vector has squared norm one. Raw indices first become a Cartesian direction through L or L^(-T).

blocks.title: validate_frame: reject stretching and reflection
blocks.explanation: Require a real 3-by-3 matrix. Evaluate it numerically, test T.T*T against the identity and test det(T) against +1 using absolute tolerance. Return the original matrix so exact symbolic forms remain available for reporting.
blocks.why: An orthogonal matrix with determinant -1 reflects handedness; it is not a proper crystal rotation. A nonorthogonal matrix also changes the geometry rather than rotating it.
blocks.check: The identity and a proper rotated basis pass. A frame obtained by reversing only one axis has determinant -1 and is rejected.

blocks.title: build_orientation: choose an explicit orientation route
blocks.explanation: Build L first. Reject a request to allow reflection. A manual-matrix route validates T_manual and returns that frame without applying hkl, uvw or ψ again. Otherwise require the hkl route.
blocks.why: A manually supplied complete frame must not be rotated a second time by inactive orientation fields. This prevents hidden geometry changes when switching input modes.
blocks.check: The returned notes identify a manual frame. On that route, changing hkl has no effect because the manual frame is the declared orientation.

blocks.title: Calculate the signed reciprocal normal
blocks.explanation: Validate normal_sign as +1 or -1 and the nonzero Miller-index vector. Compute g=L.inv().T*indices, normalize it and apply the requested sign to obtain Z.
blocks.why: A plane normal is a reciprocal-lattice direction: for an orthorhombic cell, g is proportional to (h/a0,k/b0,l/c0). The sign selects the side of the plane while leaving the plane indices unchanged.
blocks.check: Using different a0,b0,c0 changes a tilted (211) normal. A principal (100) normal remains along the corresponding Cartesian axis.

blocks.title: Choose an automatic in-plane reference when needed
blocks.explanation: If uvw is absent, select the Cartesian axis least parallel to Z, then subtract its projection along Z. Store that transverse vector and a note naming the chosen reference.
blocks.why: This gives a stable coordinate reference without claiming that the automatic X direction is a measured crystallographic in-plane direction.
blocks.check: The projected tangent is perpendicular to Z and nonzero. The notes should state that automatic X is a coordinate convention.

blocks.title: Use an explicit crystallographic in-plane direction
blocks.explanation: For a supplied uvw, validate it and form t=L*uvw. Compute the normalized residual of g.T*t. Because g=L^(-T)*hkl, this dot product is hu+kv+lw; reject directions that do not lie in the chosen plane.
blocks.why: A reference direction outside the surface cannot be used as the transverse X axis without changing its physical meaning.
blocks.check: For (211), [0,1,-1] gives 2*0+1*1+1*(-1)=0 and passes even when the lattice lengths are unequal.

blocks.title: Normalize the tangent, apply ψ and assemble T
blocks.explanation: Normalize t to X0, obtain Y0=Z cross X0 and validate ψ. Form X=cos(ψ)X0+sin(ψ)Y0 and Y=-sin(ψ)X0+cos(ψ)Y0. Stack X,Y,Z as columns, validate the proper frame and return the intermediate vectors with T.
blocks.why: The cross product fixes handedness and ψ sets the in-plane frame orientation. Saving L,g,t,X0,Y0 and T lets later mathematical reports show each construction step.
blocks.check: T.T*T is the identity and det(T)=+1. Positive ψ rotates the measurement axes X toward Y; with fixed laboratory optics, an active sample rotation has the opposite sign.

blocks.title: Confirm that this cell finished executing
blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.
blocks.check: Run Cells 1–3 in order and confirm the Cell 03/22 message. Model/source checks must be inspected separately in Validation.

pitfalls: Miller indices are not generally Cartesian normal components for a noncubic cell.
ψ is the frame angle; α and θ are optical scan variables.
The negative normal in the slide reference preserves its displayed X and Y signs in a proper frame; it does not identify the outward face of a real sample.
A manual frame bypasses hkl/uvw reconstruction, so reports must identify which input route was active.

overview: Define the symmetry-allowed full Cartesian Raman tensor library and material presets. This cell separates tensor form, phonon-component degeneracy, numerical coefficient values and historical regression policies. It defines 21 point-group templates; atomic structure and experiment still determine which phonon branches and coefficients actually occur.
workflow: Build symmetric 3-by-3 tensor templates.
Register point groups with explicit Cartesian axis settings.
Attach material mode labels and illustrative metrics.
Resolve selected families, substitute coefficients and declare how complete phonon components combine.

blocks.title: symmetric: assemble six independent Cartesian entries
blocks.explanation: Place xx,yy,zz on the diagonal and copy xy,xz,yz into the corresponding symmetric off-diagonal pairs. The result satisfies R.T=R while its coefficient symbols can still be complex.
blocks.why: The library implements the stated first-order symmetric electric-dipole tensor model. Symmetry of matrix indices does not mean the matrix is Hermitian or its coefficients are real.
blocks.check: symmetric(a,b,c,xy=d) has Rxy=Ryx=d. R.H need not equal R when d or a is complex.

blocks.title: family: preserve complete phonon partners
blocks.explanation: Store one or more component tensors as SymPy matrices, a descriptive note and component channel labels. If labels are not supplied, generate one-based labels automatically.
blocks.why: A degenerate irrep can have multiple orthogonal phonon components. Those complete component tensors need to remain distinct until their powers are combined.
blocks.check: An Ag family contains one complete tensor; the cubic T family contains three complete components.

blocks.title: Create reusable tensor forms
blocks.explanation: DIAG is diag(a,b,c). MONO_A includes xz=d and MONO_B includes xy=e,yz=f for the unique-y monoclinic setting. AXIAL is diag(a,a,b). OUTPLANE and TRIGONAL define paired tensors; CUBIC_E uses two equally normalized diagonal components and CUBIC_T uses yz,xz,xy components. Initialize an empty point-group registry.
blocks.why: Reusing an explicit template keeps equivalent point-group tensor forms consistent while retaining the axis convention and coefficient-sharing within each degenerate family.
blocks.check: Both cubic E components have equal Frobenius norm. Their overall normalization is absorbed in the coefficient; three diagonal Ag entries are not three degenerate phonons.

blocks.title: add_group: register a complete convention
blocks.explanation: Write a record containing the crystallographic symbol, crystal system, axis explanation and tensor families into POINT_GROUPS under the chosen name.
blocks.why: A tensor table without an axis setting is ambiguous: exchanging axes can exchange the labels assigned to off-diagonal irreps.
blocks.check: Each registry entry must include its axes description as well as its matrices.

blocks.title: Register triclinic C1 and Ci
blocks.explanation: Both groups permit the six independent entries of a symmetric Cartesian tensor. The mode label is A for C1 and Ag for Ci. These are general full symmetric matrices, not assumed diagonal matrices.
blocks.why: Low symmetry does not generally force a tensor principal axis to coincide with a crystallographic axis. Restricting triclinic Ag to xx,yy,zz would discard allowed terms.
blocks.check: The Ci Ag tensor contains xy=d, xz=e and yz=f in addition to a,b,c.

blocks.title: Register the monoclinic and mirror settings
blocks.explanation: Loop through C2, Cs and C2h while assigning the same stated unique-y or xz-mirror setting. Their even/A-like family uses MONO_A; their odd/B-like family uses MONO_B. The labels change with the group.
blocks.why: The loop shares matrix patterns without pretending that the irreducible-representation labels or group symbols are identical.
blocks.check: C2h Ag contains xz=d. Therefore a general Ag display for this group must retain an additional xz component.

blocks.title: Register orthorhombic D2, C2v and D2h
blocks.explanation: Assign the diagonal family and three symmetric off-diagonal families xy, xz and yz. For D2h the labels are Ag, B1g, B2g and B3g respectively, with Cartesian x,y,z aligned to a,b,c.
blocks.why: This is the tensor-form foundation for the orthorhombic CaNb2O6 model. Its diagonal Ag entries are independent complex coefficients of one phonon tensor.
blocks.check: In this setting B1g selects xy, B2g selects xz and B3g selects yz. Those labels must be reinterpreted if the crystal axes are permuted.

blocks.title: Register trigonal D3, C3v and D3d
blocks.explanation: Use AXIAL for the one-dimensional A-like family and two TRIGONAL components for E. Both E components share c and d with signs tied to the documented basal-axis setting.
blocks.why: A degenerate E doublet is a coupled representation, not two unrelated tensors whose coefficients can be chosen independently within one branch.
blocks.check: D3d provides A1g and Eg. Rotating a complete doublet basis must not change its unresolved summed power.

blocks.title: Register tetragonal D4, C4v, D2d and D4h
blocks.explanation: Populate A-like axial, B1-like diagonal difference, B2-like xy and E-like xz/yz component tensors. The principal axis is z and x,y lie in the basal plane.
blocks.why: The same symmetry categories need a consistent coefficient basis across materials, while the irrep names preserve the proper group labels.
blocks.check: The E family contains two out-of-plane components. Their extinction on a particular plane must come from projection and Jones contraction, not from deleting their 3D tensors.

blocks.title: Register hexagonal groups and the monolayer setting
blocks.explanation: D6, C6v and D6h use A, E1 and E2 categories; D3h uses A1-prime, E-double-prime and E-prime labels. The axial tensor, xz/yz pair and basal diagonal/xy pair are registered in Cartesian axes with z along c.
blocks.why: The crystallographic unit cell can be skew in the basal plane, but tensor components remain Cartesian. Monolayer and bulk labels also cannot be interchanged without checking symmetry.
blocks.check: Monolayer MoS2 uses D3h A1-prime and E-prime. A D6h E1g family is not the same irrep as E2g.

blocks.title: Register cubic Td and Oh
blocks.explanation: Use an isotropic a*I tensor for the A-like template, the two CUBIC_E components for E and the three CUBIC_T components for T2. Keep the conventional [100],[010],[001] Cartesian axes.
blocks.why: Silicon first-order scattering uses the Oh T2g triplet. A point-group template is broader than a material mode list: not every listed template must occur as a phonon in every material.
blocks.check: The Si material below selects T2g only. Its three phonon-component intensities are retained even though an individual component can be dark in a selected geometry.

blocks.title: Record primary source roles
blocks.explanation: SOURCES stores titles, links and the specific role of each reference: tensor tables, cubic geometry, transition-metal-dichalcogenide assignments and the parent TiS2 model. A link is documentation metadata and is not used to calculate coefficients.
blocks.why: A reproducible library should distinguish a symmetry source from a material-specific spectrum or line-shape study.
blocks.check: Source roles should match what the program actually implements. A spectral shoulder or Fano profile is not automatically a new first-order tensor mode.

blocks.title: CaNb2O6 preset
blocks.explanation: Register Pbcn/D2h with Ag and the three Bg tensor types. Use a unity metric and (211) as an explicitly illustrative slide-reference starting point. The note instructs the user to enter actual lattice lengths for a physical tilted-surface normal.
blocks.why: The preset reproduces a coordinate reference without pretending that CaNb2O6 is cubic or that the unity lattice lengths are measured crystal parameters.
blocks.check: For a physical tilted CaNb2O6 surface, replace the length ratios. The general application separates Ag component plots and keeps the complete coherent result in an audit.

blocks.title: Silicon preset
blocks.explanation: Register the diamond structure Fd-3m/Oh, selecting the T2g triplet on a principal starting surface. Its three T2g components are unresolved orthogonal phonons in the implemented benchmark.
blocks.why: Silicon provides a published orientation benchmark with a complete degenerate component set, distinct from the Cartesian decomposition of one Ag tensor.
blocks.check: A unity cubic metric preserves the correct surface-normal direction because a common lattice-length scale cancels on normalization.

blocks.title: Excess-Ti TiS2 parent preset
blocks.explanation: Register D3d A1g and Eg as a parent 1T structure model. The note explicitly distinguishes this symmetry model from excess-Ti disorder, shoulder features, two-phonon processes and Breit-Wigner-Fano line shapes.
blocks.why: A first-order Γ-point tensor should not claim to calculate every feature of a nonstoichiometric material spectrum.
blocks.check: Use a lower symmetry or a more detailed response model when the sample phase requires it; the listed c/a ratio is illustrative.

blocks.title: Bulk 2H-NbSe2 preset
blocks.explanation: Register bulk D6h with A1g, E1g and two E2g branches. The two E2g entries refer to different phonon branches and therefore have independent coefficient dictionaries.
blocks.why: Sharing an irrep does not force two different phonons to share numerical tensor coefficients, and a monolayer or charge-density-wave phase can require another symmetry model.
blocks.check: Changing the coefficients of E2g_low must not silently change E2g_high.

blocks.title: 1T-VSe2 parent preset

blocks.title: General material and default coefficient values
blocks.explanation: GENERAL leaves branch counts and frequencies unspecified and enables point-group templates or a custom tensor. DEFAULT_VALUES supplies illustrative a=1,b=4/5,c=3/5 and unit off-diagonal coefficients.

overview: Define the actual incident, analyzer and sample-detection Jones states for each optical protocol. The optical method is a physical-input choice independent of the material. The effective detector is e_s=B.H*e_an, so a return optic can change the measurement even when two configurations share circular endpoints. The optical-profile guide explains physical differences without changing the intensity engine.
workflow: Define orthonormal linear and circular bases.
Construct ideal rotation and waveplate matrices.
Build the selected input, return optic and analyzer.
Return the effective sample detector and the correct scan-harmonic basis.

blocks.title: Define laboratory bases and the transverse selector
blocks.explanation: x_hat and y_hat are the laboratory transverse unit vectors. sig_p=(1,I)/sqrt(2) and sig_m=(1,-I)/sqrt(2) form a fixed-laboratory circular basis. P selects laboratory X and Y from a 3D vector.
blocks.why: The full crystal tensor is rotated before P is applied. Crystal-z entries can contribute to transverse laboratory fields on a tilted surface, so P is not permission to discard the crystal-z tensor row at the start.
blocks.check: sig_p.H*sig_m is zero and each circular vector has norm one. P has shape 2-by-3.

blocks.title: rot: two-dimensional active rotation
blocks.explanation: Return the real orthogonal matrix [[cos(t),-sin(t)],[sin(t),cos(t)]]. Positive t rotates the x direction toward y in the fixed laboratory plane.
blocks.why: An optical element whose axes are rotated needs a coordinate transformation into and out of its principal-axis basis.
blocks.check: rot(t).T*rot(t) is the identity and rot(π/2)*x_hat equals y_hat.

blocks.title: waveplate and the adopted QWP matrices
blocks.explanation: waveplate constructs Rot(θ)*diag(1,exp(I*γ))*Rot(θ).T. The selected plate has axis -45 degrees and retardance π/2. The adopted reverse-path matrix is the transpose of that plate, following the imported source convention.
blocks.why: A quarter-wave retardance changes relative phase rather than merely rotating a linear vector. The reverse-path convention must be declared with the chosen fixed coordinate bases.
blocks.check: The chosen Q is unitary and symmetric and Q*x_hat is σ⁺ up to a global phase. Q.T is not being asserted as a universal return matrix for every optical arrangement.

blocks.title: jones: normalized general polarization state
blocks.explanation: Construct e(θ,β)=(cos(θ),exp(I*β)*sin(θ)). θ controls the component amplitudes and β their relative phase. Both angles are in radians at this function boundary.
blocks.why: One expression covers linear, circular and elliptical pure states without redefining the scattering law for each material.
blocks.check: β=0 yields a linear state. θ=π/4,β=π/2 yields σ⁺. A general β or unequal amplitudes generally gives an ellipse.

blocks.title: Name the optical protocols
blocks.explanation: OPTICS_LABELS maps internal protocol identifiers to readable labels for QWP, direct Jones, circular, linear and cubic-reference configurations. These names do not themselves select coefficients or align plots.
blocks.why: Readable labels must remain tied to explicit Jones definitions below. A common label such as σ⁺α does not guarantee identical detector states in different conventions.
blocks.check: The cubic-reference labels identify Section 2.2. Use the explicit matrices below as the mathematical definition and the linked reference section for the surrounding tensor and intensity equations.

blocks.title: optical_chain: initialize an explicit protocol
blocks.explanation: The function accepts a protocol identifier and optional direct-state or paper-control dictionaries. The default FIRST basis means a fixed incident state with a first-harmonic analyzer amplitude; analyzers is initially absent unless a paired linear scan needs both detectors.
blocks.why: A single optical-state record lets the same tensor contraction serve every material and report actual active parameters instead of reading disabled controls.
blocks.check: Unknown protocol names raise an error. The returned scan_basis must describe whether the amplitude uses FIRST, SECOND or CONSTANT harmonics.

blocks.title: QWP chain: sample input and analyzer after return optics
blocks.explanation: Set E_i=Q*x_hat, B=Q.T and e_an=(-sin(α),cos(α)). The α=0 analyzer direction is +Y after the return plate; α=90 degrees is -X. Store this origin convention explicitly.
blocks.why: The measured amplitude is e_an.H*B*R_perp*E_i. Removing B while keeping the same analyzer vector would describe another experiment.
blocks.check: The effective sample detector is Q.conjugate()*e_an because B.H=(Q.T).H. Its projectors at intermediate angles differ from the elliptical-reference scan.

blocks.title: Elliptical reference scan
blocks.explanation: Set E_i=σ⁺, B=I and e_s=e_an=(cos(π/4+α),I*sin(π/4+α)). This directly specifies the detector state at the sample, with fixed relative phase π/2.
blocks.why: This reproduces the declared reference Jones states, including their continuous intermediate elliptical states. It is not inferred from a rotating linear analyzer after the adopted QWP.
blocks.check: At α=0 the detector is σ⁺; at α=π/2 it is σ⁻ up to a global sign. At intermediate α its projector differs from the QWP branch.

blocks.title: Custom direct Jones states
blocks.explanation: Require four angles: θᵢ,βᵢ,θₛ₀,βₛ. Convert and validate them, then build the fixed input e(θᵢ,βᵢ), identity return matrix and scanned detector e(θₛ₀+α,βₛ).
blocks.why: Explicit custom states permit controlled equivalence tests: the reference scan is recovered with (45,90,45,90) degrees, while a direct linear detector uses βₛ=0.
blocks.check: The custom branch represents this four-parameter direct-state family. It does not automatically reproduce an arbitrary return optic whose effective detector has a different α dependence.

blocks.title: Circular input with direct-linear or fixed-circular detection
blocks.explanation: Validate s_in as +1 or -1 and choose the corresponding circular input. With CIRCULAR_LINEAR, scan a direct linear detector at α plus its declared zero offset. With CIRCULAR_SAME or CIRCULAR_OPPOSITE, choose a fixed circular detector and mark the amplitude CONSTANT. Record that the quantitative curve is the ℓ=0 plane-wave calculation.
blocks.why: A fixed circular channel is one projection, not a rotating-analyzer experiment. An OAM selection-rule input must not silently modify these plane-wave intensities.
blocks.check: Fixed circular intensity is independent of α. Changing analyzer_zero_deg rotates the direct-linear scan origin but does not change the underlying tensor.

blocks.title: Co-rotating linear VV/VH states
blocks.explanation: Set angle=α+θ₀. The incident state is (cos(angle),sin(angle)); the parallel detector is identical and the crossed detector is (-sin(angle),cos(angle)). Select the required detector, retain both for LINEAR_PAIR and mark the amplitude SECOND.
blocks.why: Both input and detector rotate, so the amplitude contains constant and second angular harmonics and the intensity can contain fourth harmonics. VV and VH together must share one coefficient set.
blocks.check: The two detector vectors are orthogonal. A standalone VV curve must match the VV member of LINEAR_PAIR for identical input values and angle zero.

blocks.title: Return the effective detector and active parameters
blocks.explanation: Reject an unsupported kind. Return kind, label, active parameters, E_i, B, e_an and e_s=B.H*e_an together with the scan basis and optional paired analyzers.
blocks.why: The identity e_an.H*B=e_s.H makes the return-optic chain and the direct sample-state contraction equivalent. The Hermitian transpose is essential for a complex detector state.
blocks.check: For any resolved tensor, e_an.H*B*R_perp*E_i and effective_analyzer.H*R_perp*E_i must agree. Replacing .H with .T generally fails for circular or elliptical detection.

overview: Implement the shared matrix-to-amplitude-to-intensity engine. Full 3D crystal tensors rotate first, transverse optical states contract with the rotated tensor, and complex amplitudes are squared only after that contraction. Continuous extrema come from exact harmonic forms rather than a fitted polar pattern or a coarse angular grid.
workflow: Rotate R_c into the measurement frame and project the external transverse field.
Calculate the detected complex amplitude through the declared return optics.
Extract the mathematically allowed amplitude harmonics.
Substitute numerical coefficients, evaluate powers and determine analytic-harmonic extrema.

blocks.title: transverse_amplitude_record: propagate the field
blocks.explanation: Validate a 2-by-2 transverse tensor. Form E_sc=R_perp*E_i and E_out=B*E_sc, retaining symbolic complex entries. Read the declared amplitude scan basis from the optical record.
blocks.why: Matrix order follows the physical chain. This helper performs shared linear algebra; it does not choose a material, a rotation or a rule for combining different phonon final states.
blocks.check: E_sc and E_out remain two-component complex vectors. Intensity has not yet been formed or substituted for a tensor entry.

blocks.title: Keep fixed-channel amplitudes constant
blocks.explanation: For SECOND or CONSTANT profiles, explicitly contract e_an.H*E_out. If the profile is CONSTANT, return that scalar as K0 with the intermediate fields and no angular harmonics.
blocks.why: A fixed circular detector should not acquire an artificial α dependence from the plotting grid.
blocks.check: Its intensity curve is a circle of radius |K0|^2 on an intensity polar plot, or zero when K0 vanishes.

blocks.title: Derive co-rotating linear amplitude coefficients
blocks.explanation: The allowed amplitude form is K0+Kc*cos(2*α)+Ks*sin(2*α). Evaluate the matrix amplitude at 0 and π/2 to obtain K0 and Kc; evaluate at π/4 to obtain Ks. Store these coefficients and the reconstructed exact harmonic amplitude.
blocks.why: These evaluations extract coefficients of a known algebraic basis, rather than fitting a target curve. Squaring this amplitude later automatically retains second and fourth intensity harmonics.
blocks.check: The reconstructed amplitude should agree with the direct Jones matrix chain at independently chosen angles, including complex tensor coefficients.

blocks.title: Derive fixed-input analyzer coefficients
blocks.explanation: For FIRST profiles, project the outgoing field on the analyzer at 0 and π/2 to obtain C and D. Store A(α)=C*cos(α)+D*sin(α), its coefficients and the intermediate fields.
blocks.why: The declared detector family is linear in cos(α),sin(α). Keeping its complex coefficients intact preserves interference between the two analyzer contributions.
blocks.check: A direct evaluation at an intermediate angle must equal the C,D reconstruction. C and D are generally complex even if some geometry entries are real.

blocks.title: amplitude_record: rotate the full crystal tensor first
blocks.explanation: Require a 3-by-3 R_c, form R_lab=T.T*R_c*T, then R_perp=P*R_lab*P.T. Embed the incident Jones state into three dimensions using P.T and record the complete induced polarization R_lab*E_i,lab. Call the transverse helper and retain R_c,R_lab and the 3D fields with its amplitude record.
blocks.why: Crystal-z coefficients can enter transverse laboratory scattering on tilted planes. The induced polarization may have a Z component, but the collected ideal external plane wave is transverse.
blocks.check: A direct crystal-coordinate contraction using T*P.T*E_i and T*P.T*e_s must reproduce the projected amplitude. Tensor coefficients stay linear until the final power.

blocks.title: numeric_terms: substitute only the amplitude coefficients
blocks.explanation: Choose C,D, K0,Kc,Ks or K0 according to each term record. Substitute the selected mode values once, reject unresolved symbols, convert the resolved coefficients to complex NumPy values and reject non-finite results or an empty term set.
blocks.why: The angular grid can then be evaluated efficiently by matrix multiplication without repeatedly substituting every tensor entry at every angle.
blocks.check: FIRST returns one two-coefficient row per term, SECOND returns three and CONSTANT returns one. No tensor coefficient symbol should remain.

blocks.title: Derive all VV/VH intensity harmonics
blocks.explanation: For A=K0+Kc*cos(2θ)+Ks*sin(2θ), calculate I0, Ic, Is, I4c and I4s using powers and conjugate cross products. Sum these terms across the declared orthogonal phonon components. Reject overflow and identify a numerically constant result using a relative harmonic threshold.
blocks.why: Complex coefficient phases contribute through real parts of products such as K0*Kc.conjugate(). Keeping the fourth harmonics is necessary for general co-rotating linear scans.
blocks.check: The coefficients reconstruct the same nonnegative intensity as direct |A|^2. A constant channel has no unique maximum-angle label.

blocks.title: Solve the continuous stationary-angle equation
blocks.explanation: Set z=exp(2i*θ), u1=(Ic-i*Is)/2 and u2=(I4c-i*I4s)/2. The derivative becomes a quartic with coefficients [2u2,u1,0,-u1*, -2u2*]. Remove leading zeros, find roots and retain unit-circle roots. Convert their phases to candidate angles modulo π and evaluate the harmonic intensity at those angles.
blocks.why: A 0.5-degree display grid is not an accurate method for locating every maximum or minimum. The stationary polynomial uses the calculated intensity law itself.
blocks.check: Candidate roots must lie on the unit circle within the stated tolerance. Failure to resolve stationary angles raises an error rather than returning a guessed plot maximum.

blocks.title: Report extrema with roundoff-aware positivity
blocks.explanation: Choose the largest and smallest candidate intensities, estimate a floating-point positivity tolerance and reject a negative minimum beyond that tolerance. Clamp only a roundoff-sized negative minimum to zero, then return all harmonic coefficients, extrema and corresponding angles in degrees.
blocks.why: Physical intensity is nonnegative, but finite numerical cancellation can produce a tiny negative reported extremum at an exact extinction. The check distinguishes that numerical artifact from a substantial algebraic error.
blocks.check: A meaningful negative minimum must fail. Extrema should agree with a sufficiently dense independent angular evaluation without depending on the chosen display sampling.

blocks.title: summary_for_amplitudes: dispatch by the declared basis size
blocks.explanation: Three amplitude coefficients invoke the 0/2/4-harmonic summary. One coefficient gives a constant sum of phonon-component intensities. Two coefficients invoke the FIRST-basis summary.
blocks.why: The same numerical result structure supports a fixed circular channel, an analyzer scan and VV/VH without forcing them into one incorrect angular formula.
blocks.check: A constant summary has Imin=Imax and no preferred angle; a FIRST summary has no fourth-harmonic coefficients.

blocks.title: intensity_expression: build the displayed harmonic law
blocks.explanation: Construct I0+Ic*cos(2var)+Is*sin(2var), adding I4c*cos(4var)+I4s*sin(4var) when those coefficients exist. Missing fourth harmonics default to zero. The variable can be α or the displayed θ symbol.
blocks.why: Mathematical reports and exports must show every harmonic actually calculated, using the scan label associated with the optical configuration.
blocks.check: Substituting numerical summary values and angles must reproduce the corresponding intensity array to numerical precision.

blocks.title: summary_from_pairs: expand first-harmonic amplitudes
blocks.explanation: For each C,D row, form |C|^2, |D|^2 and Re(C*D.conjugate()). Sum component contributions and set I0=(|C|^2+|D|^2)/2, Ic=(|C|^2-|D|^2)/2 and Is=Re(CD*). Compute δ=hypot(Ic,Is), then reject overflow or non-finite coefficients.
blocks.why: The cross term follows from the complex squared modulus. Adding |C*cos(α)|^2 and |D*sin(α)|^2 alone would omit interference within the detected amplitude.
blocks.check: A controlled relative phase can change Is while preserving |C| and |D|. This must change the polar pattern in the way predicted by the complex contraction.

blocks.title: summary_from_pairs: analytic extrema and constant channels
blocks.explanation: Use Imin=I0-δ and Imax=I0+δ, with a roundoff-aware nonnegativity test. A negligible δ marks a constant channel. Otherwise obtain alpha_max=atan2(Is,Ic)/2 modulo 180 degrees and alpha_min=alpha_max+90 degrees modulo 180.
blocks.why: These are continuous-angle extrema of the exact two-harmonic intensity form, not maxima of a sampled data array.
blocks.check: For I=1+sin(2α), the maximum is at 45 degrees. A constant intensity must not be assigned a fabricated unique peak angle.

blocks.title: evaluate_terms: calculate sampled intensities
blocks.explanation: Obtain numerical amplitude coefficient rows. Build the appropriate angular basis array, multiply rows by that basis, square the complex modulus of each resulting amplitude and sum the declared term powers. Reject overflow or non-finite values and return amplitude coefficients, individual powers, total and harmonic summary.
blocks.why: Coherent tensor-entry interference has already occurred inside each amplitude record. This sum is over the selected complete phonon terms; the later general Ag display calls this same engine for each component separately.
blocks.check: For one complete tensor, total is simply its one |A|^2 array. For an unresolved degenerate family, total contains the sum of complete-component powers.

blocks.title: Convenience wrappers for independent checks
blocks.explanation: numeric_curve returns the total intensity from evaluate_terms for an explicitly supplied angular array. numeric_summary returns continuous harmonic extrema directly from the substituted amplitude coefficients.
blocks.why: Tests and small scripted examples can reuse exactly the production definitions without depending on GUI widgets or a plotted figure.
blocks.check: Changing only the display grid should change the sampling density, not the analytic maximum angle returned by numeric_summary.

Retain independently derived intensity terms for validation, then validate source input values.

blocks.title: Define the effective source tensor and workflow identifiers
blocks.explanation: Declare separate real a,A,δ,φ symbols. Build R=[[a,A*exp(i*δ)],[-A*exp(i*δ),a*exp(i*φ)]], name the source mode and map internal workflow/model identifiers to readable labels. The off-diagonal signs are those of this imported effective model.
blocks.why: Reusing the general complex a symbol would change the source algebra assumptions. The source antisymmetric off-diagonal pair also must not be silently imposed on a nonmagnetic symmetric D2h material tensor.
blocks.check: At φ=0 the diagonal entries coincide. At A=0 the model becomes diagonal. This source model has no crystal-surface parameter.

blocks.title: qwp_source_algebra: cache the fixed symbolic calculation
blocks.explanation: lru_cache(maxsize=1) stores this parameter-independent symbolic result after its first evaluation. Build the QWP optical chain, call the same transverse amplitude engine and calculate R++=<σ⁺|R|σ⁺> and R-+=<σ⁻|R|σ⁺>.
blocks.why: The symbolic source structure is fixed; repeatedly rebuilding it for every numerical slider value would waste time. Numerical coefficient values are substituted after retrieving this symbolic record.
blocks.check: The source record amplitude comes from the actual matrix chain. Cached expressions remain symbolic in the four real source parameters.

blocks.title: Reconstruct the source analyzer reference and relative phase
blocks.explanation: Pass both circular basis states through the return QWP. Remove a global phase from the dominant σ⁺ output component to construct a real reference axis, rotate that axis by +90 degrees, project the σ⁻ output onto the perpendicular axis and build the scanned analyzer. Check it against the optical_chain analyzer.
blocks.why: The angle zero and phase ratio determine the interference sign. An analyzer measured from laboratory X is not automatically the same convention as an analyzer measured from the returned σ⁺ axis.
blocks.check: The source reference is +Y, its perpendicular direction is -X and the reconstructed analyzer equals (-sin(α),cos(α)).

blocks.title: Compute circular-channel powers and their interference
blocks.explanation: Calculate |R++|^2, |R-+|^2 and Im(R++*R-+.conjugate()) directly from the symbolic circular amplitudes using the real source parameter assumptions.
blocks.why: In this adopted return-optic chain, the relative QWP phase turns the analyzer interference coefficient into the imaginary part of the circular-amplitude product.
blocks.check: These independently computed terms must agree with the source formulas built in the next block.

blocks.title: Build an independent closed-form source reference
blocks.explanation: Construct reference_pp=a^2*cos(φ/2)^2+A^2+2aA*cos(φ/2)*sin(φ/2-δ), reference_mp=a^2*sin(φ/2)^2 and the corresponding cross coefficient. Form the source intensity as reference_pp*cos(α)^2+reference_mp*sin(α)^2+2*reference_cross*sin(α)*cos(α).
blocks.why: A separately stated analytic law provides a useful regression target. It is retained for checks and reporting while the production amplitude still comes from matrix multiplication.
blocks.check: With φ=0, R-+ vanishes. With A=0 the result reduces to a^2*cos(α-φ/2)^2 in the adopted convention.

blocks.title: Return all source intermediates
blocks.explanation: Return the production record, circular amplitudes, returned circular vectors, phase factors, analyzer axes, directly calculated powers and independent source intensity pieces in one dictionary.
blocks.why: A calculation can be inspected stage by stage rather than judged only by its final polar curve.
blocks.check: Reports should identify whether a value is a production matrix result or an independent source reference; neither may be mixed with the slide-specific component prescription.

blocks.title: qwp_source_values: validate and substitute source parameters
blocks.explanation: Require a,A,delta_deg,phi_deg, validate each as a finite real number and convert the input decimals to rationals. Map the two amplitudes to their source symbols and convert phase degrees to radians.
blocks.why: The imported source makes the amplitudes real and locates complex character in explicit phases. Its substitution dictionary must use those same symbols and units.
blocks.check: An incomplete parameter dictionary raises an error. A 90-degree δ substitutes π/2, not the number 90 inside exp(i*δ).

blocks.title: Confirm that this cell finished executing
blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.

The alternative convention in the source appendix is not silently substituted for the adopted main chain.
The cached symbolic expressions must be evaluated with source parameters, not the general crystal coefficient dictionary.
A 3D material extension preserves the chosen QWP optical sequence while supplying a rotated symmetry-allowed crystal tensor.

overview: Attach reference conventions, illustrative material examples and conditional circular selection diagnostics to the existing engine. The complex-linear reference supplies phase-sensitive VV/VH examples; the circular-selection reference supplies necessary angular-momentum congruences with stated scope. These congruences do not predict a quantitative vortex-beam intensity.
workflow: Record reference roles and extend the material library.
Build explicit linear and circular demonstration configurations.
Validate integer selection-rule controls and transform tensors into the circular basis.
Report plane-wave channels and conditional selection checks separately.
Offer a supplied-term resonance utility without inferring microscopic parameters.

blocks.title: Identify the scan symbol and reference roles
blocks.explanation: Declare θ as a real display symbol. PAPER_SOURCES records the two reference titles, DOIs, relevant equation ranges and documented scope, then merges them into SOURCES. The calculation still uses the explicit state and tensor definitions; citation metadata does not choose the optical method.
blocks.why: A linear-polarization intensity formalism and an angular-momentum selection rule answer different questions. The program must not promote a necessary circular rule into a universal quantitative scattering law.
blocks.check: The circular source role points to DOI 10.1039/D1CP02209A, while complex-linear scans point to DOI 10.1039/D1CP03626B.

blocks.title: Extend the library with black phosphorus
blocks.explanation: Add a D2h example with layer plane xz, surface normal y and separate Ag(1),B2g,Ag(2) branches. The lattice is a unity principal-plane reference; the dedicated reference factory below supplies the printed coefficient ratios.
blocks.why: The same group label D2h can use an axis setting different from an intuitive xy layer drawing. The axes must match the equations being reproduced.
blocks.check: The chosen (010) geometry projects the xz tensor subspace. The two Ag branches retain independent coefficient dictionaries.

blocks.title: Extend the library with monolayer MoS2
blocks.explanation: Add the D3h A1-prime and E-prime branches with a conventional hexagonal cell. The note identifies the preset as a plane-wave Jones example and uses monolayer irrep names.
blocks.why: Bulk-like A1g/E2g names appearing in a reference passage must not replace the correct monolayer D3h labels in the material library.
blocks.check: The preset is MoS2-1L, not a bulk D6h material. Its coefficients remain illustrative.

blocks.title: Extend the library with graphene
blocks.explanation: Add a monolayer D6h G-mode example mapped to E2g. Supply the conventional hexagonal metric and a note that neither electronic bands nor vortex intensity are inferred.
blocks.why: A known Raman irrep is sufficient to demonstrate a polarization contraction, but not sufficient to compute all microscopic optical transitions.
blocks.check: The G family retains both E2g components and their shared branch coefficient.

blocks.title: Extend the library with monoclinic 1T-prime MoTe2
blocks.explanation: Add C2h Ag and Bg in the unique-y convention, using an illustrative monoclinic β angle of 100 degrees. The note distinguishes the chosen inputs from measured fit parameters in the cited figure.
blocks.why: Nonorthogonal crystallographic axes require the lattice metric, while the tensor remains expressed in an orthonormal Cartesian frame.
blocks.check: The monoclinic Ag template contains an allowed xz entry; it is not forced into an orthorhombic diagonal tensor.

blocks.title: Extend the library with ReSe2
blocks.explanation: Add a Ci Ag example in Cartesian tensor axes, with an illustrative metric and a note requiring measured triclinic cell parameters and mode-specific coefficients for a sample calculation.
blocks.why: A fully populated symmetric tensor is allowed by Ci. A material dropdown alone cannot determine its orientation, principal axes or numerical coefficients.
blocks.check: The full Ci Ag family exposes all six independent symmetric entries.

blocks.title: default_paper_parameters: keep controls explicit
blocks.explanation: Return circular-rule defaults for the CIRCULAR workflow: s_in=+1, N=2, zero incident OAM, one zero phonon charge, no absorption charge and unestablished thin-2D assumptions. Linear and cubic workflows receive a zero scan-angle offset. Other workflows receive no paper-parameter dictionary here.
blocks.why: A workflow should not inherit another reference calculation merely because a hidden control retains an old value.
blocks.check: The general pipeline later merges these defaults with explicitly supplied active parameters. The assumptions checkbox is false by default.

blocks.title: paper_demo_config: build a declared reference workflow
blocks.explanation: Validate the requested CIRCULAR or LINEAR method, obtain a material demonstration configuration and replace its workflow policy with a coherent full-tensor rule and the selected direct circular-linear or paired-linear optical profile. Add explicit reference and illustrative-input notes.
blocks.why: The tensor library and scattering engine remain shared, while the reference-specific input set remains inspectable. Creating a demonstration does not certify its coefficients as measured material constants.
blocks.check: A LINEAR demonstration uses LINEAR_PAIR; a CIRCULAR demonstration uses CIRCULAR_LINEAR. Both retain coherent complete phonon tensors.

blocks.title: linear_bp_reference_config: enter published example ratios
blocks.explanation: Load the BP linear example, choose the declared normal side and enter separate Ag ratios c/a=1.96 with zero relative phase and c/a=1.32 with 94-degree relative phase. Enter the off-diagonal branch reference magnitude 1.30. The library xz coefficient is e even though the review names that entry f.
blocks.why: Reproducing a reference formula requires its coefficient ratio, phase, plane and angle convention, not only the material name or a visually similar curve.
blocks.check: The examples reproduce the stated coherent Eq. 13 convention; they are not digitized fits to all experimental points. The global a=1 scale is arbitrary for each illustrative branch.

blocks.title: circular_mos2_reference_config: declare the plane-wave example
blocks.explanation: Load the monolayer circular-channel example, label its intensity model as ell_i=0 and set the cyclic order to 3 with phonon charges 0,+2,-2. Mark the reference assumptions as declared for this example.
blocks.why: The polarization contractions demonstrate A1-prime and E-prime channels while the charge list supports a separate necessary-congruence diagnostic.
blocks.check: Changing an OAM charge later affects the rule check only; it does not turn the plane-wave intensity into a quantitative vortex calculation.

blocks.title: circular_integer: require true integer charges
blocks.explanation: Reject Python and NumPy Booleans, require a finite real scalar and verify that converting it to int does not change its value. Return that integer.
blocks.why: Modulo-N angular-momentum conditions are defined for integer charges. Accepting True as 1 or truncating 1.5 to 1 would silently change a selection-rule input.
blocks.check: 2 and 2.0 are accepted; True and 1.5 are rejected.

blocks.title: circular_congruence: validate the discrete rule inputs
blocks.explanation: Validate N and incident/scattered circular labels as integers. Restrict N to the implemented 2,3,4,6 orders and the two circular labels to +/-1. Validate incident OAM and require at least one integer phonon charge.
blocks.why: The congruence is a discrete symmetry condition under the assumptions of the reference. Invalid labels cannot be interpreted as an elliptical state or rounded into a valid charge.
blocks.check: A missing phonon-charge list or an unsupported cyclic order gives an error before a pass/fail statement is generated.

blocks.title: circular_congruence: test necessary conservation and absorption
blocks.explanation: For each phonon charge q, test (s_s-s_i-ell_i+q) mod N=0. If an electronic absorption charge difference is supplied, also test (delta_m-s_i-ell_i) mod N=0. Return matching charges, both pass indicators and whether absorption was actually checked.
blocks.why: A conservation congruence can pass while an optical subprocess is forbidden or an assumed symmetry axis is absent. The output therefore records necessary conditions instead of claiming an intensity or a sufficient scattering rule.
blocks.check: If absorption_delta_m is omitted, combined_necessary_pass is None rather than a fabricated complete pass. Each phonon charge is tested separately.

blocks.title: circular_basis_matrix: change the optical basis
blocks.explanation: Build U with σ⁺ and σ⁻ as columns and return U.H*R_perp*U. Rows correspond to the outgoing circular basis and columns to the incident circular basis.
blocks.why: Changing basis is a representation change of the same tensor contraction, not a new material response or a different intensity prescription.
blocks.check: The circular-basis amplitude for transformed states must equal the original Cartesian-basis amplitude. The Hermitian transpose is required because U is complex unitary.

blocks.title: circular_diagnostics: keep rules and intensities separate
blocks.explanation: Read the explicit paper parameters, copy them into a diagnostic record and state the plane-wave intensity scope. Independently test the necessary rule for both outgoing circular labels and append those results.
blocks.why: Requested vortex charge must not silently mask or rescale a plane-wave Jones curve. The user needs to see which assumptions were declared and which rules were actually evaluated.
blocks.check: The scope says whether thin-2D/electronic assumptions were declared. The selected intensity arrays are not modified by this function.

blocks.title: Compute complete circular channel matrices and powers
blocks.explanation: For each selected mode, transform every production term R_perp into the circular basis, substitute the same coefficient values and accumulate absolute-squared matrix entries over the declared component tensors. Save the matrices, powers and row/column labels.
blocks.why: This gives all four circular input/output channels from the same tensor used elsewhere and preserves the distinction between within-tensor amplitude interference and component-power addition.
blocks.check: For a single term, each matrix entry is one complete circular amplitude. Matrix element phases remain available separately from the tabulated powers.

blocks.title: Check the cyclic axis for orthorhombic and monoclinic settings
blocks.explanation: Inspect the actual Cartesian Z column of T. D2/D2h require a principal Cartesian normal and N=2. C2v uses its unique z C2 axis; C2/C2h use the unique y axis. Save compatibility and its convention note.
blocks.why: A tilted (211) surface normal in D2h is not automatically a twofold rotation axis. Selecting N=2 in a dropdown does not create that symmetry about the beam direction.
blocks.check: An orthorhombic principal-axis orientation can pass this axis check; a general tilted normal does not receive an extinction prediction from it.

blocks.title: Check higher cyclic axes or report uncertified cases
blocks.explanation: For supported trigonal, tetragonal and hexagonal settings, require Z along crystallographic z and an order dividing the implemented principal rotation order. Other groups receive an explicit unknown/uncertified axis record.
blocks.why: The reference rule depends on an actual cyclic symmetry operation about the chosen axis. The program must not infer that operation from a generic hkl label alone.
blocks.check: A compatible basal normal in a D3 setting supports order 3; a tilted normal does not. Unknown axis certification is not a proof that physical scattering is forbidden.

blocks.title: State the final applicability scope
blocks.explanation: Mark the rule applicable only when the declared thin-2D assumptions and cyclic-axis compatibility are both true. If the axis is incompatible, replace the scope message with a formal-congruence-only statement and return the diagnostic record.
blocks.why: A formal congruence result has a narrower meaning than a physically established extinction rule. Explicit scope prevents a bulk tilted-crystal example from being overinterpreted.
blocks.check: Passing eq24_pass alone must not override rule_applicable=False.

blocks.title: resonance_element: validate supplied energy inputs
blocks.explanation: Convert the laser-energy grid to a NumPy array, validate a nonnegative phonon energy and require finite excitation energies. Initialize a complex result array with the same shape.
blocks.why: This utility evaluates a supplied finite resonance sum. Symmetry, a band-gap number or a material label does not provide the missing microscopic matrix elements.
blocks.check: All energies and damping parameters must use the same unit; the function interface names eV. No resonance terms produces a zero supplied-term sum.

blocks.title: Evaluate complex third-order resonance denominators
blocks.explanation: For each supplied contribution, read the two transition energies, two positive damping values and a finite complex numerator weight. Add weight/[(E_L-Ecv+i*Gamma_c)*(E_L-Ephonon-Ecprime_v+i*Gamma_cprime)] to the result and return the complex array.
blocks.why: Finite damping regularizes resonance denominators and complex weights allow phase-sensitive interference between supplied terms. These values represent external microscopic input rather than a prediction from the tensor library.
blocks.check: The returned object is a complex response element versus excitation energy, not its squared intensity. Relative phase among contributions can change both its magnitude and argument.

N=2 congruence alone often cannot distinguish circular channels and cannot replace the tensor calculation.
The layer-plane and axis conventions must match the reference equations before interpreting a VV/VH comparison.
The resonance utility requires supplied energies, broadenings and complex numerator weights; these are not inferred from the material dropdown.

overview: Independent audits test the Jones states and complete-tensor interference without changing the selected calculation.
workflow: Sample exact fields on the angle grid.
Classify their sample polarization with normalized Stokes parameters.
Transform input and detector fields into crystal coordinates and reconstruct entry amplitudes independently.
Separate entry self-powers from coherent within-phonon interference.
Attach and report audit evidence with an explicit numerical-error bound.

blocks.title: Scope of this code section
blocks.explanation:
Independent polarization-state and within-mode interference diagnostics.

The diagnostics do not choose coefficients, align a polar plot, or replace
the selected intensity curve. They make the consequences of that selection
visible and test the coherent result by a second, entry-wise calculation.
blocks.why: This module-level documentation identifies the responsibility of the following definitions and prevents confusing reference/report helpers with the active calculation engine.
blocks.check: Documentation does not execute a calculation or select coefficients.

blocks.title: PAPER_EQUATION_MAP — Attach equation provenance
blocks.explanation: The text maps complex-response tensor contraction and phase interference to DOI 10.1039/D1CP03626B, and the conditional circular rule to DOI 10.1039/D1CP02209A. It is report metadata, not an input to an intensity formula.
blocks.why: A checking program should state which physical claim each source supports. A selection-rule reference cannot be used as a numerical intensity formula.
blocks.check: Changing prose here must not change a calculated curve.

blocks.title: vector_samples — Evaluate an exact field on the angular grid
blocks.explanation: First convert the angle input into a floating NumPy array. For each symbolic field component, lambdify creates a NumPy evaluator; broadcast_to also expands an angle-independent scalar into a full angular row. vstack then returns a dimension-by-angle complex array. The final finite-value test rejects an invalid numerical field.
blocks.why: Independent audits need all field components in the same array shape even when a circular state is constant. Keeping dtype=complex preserves phase and makes conjugate products reliable.
blocks.check: A fixed two-component circular vector should return a 2-by-N array with identical columns, and a rotating real analyzer should return two angle-dependent rows.

blocks.title: normalized_stokes — Classify the actual polarization state
blocks.explanation: The function reshapes one field into two components and obtains its norm with vdot, which conjugates the first vector. It then evaluates S1=(|Ex|²−|Ey|²)/S0, S2=2Re(Ex*Ey)/S0 and S3=2Im(Ex*Ey)/S0. A tolerance identifies circular, linear or intermediate elliptical states.
blocks.why: A menu label is insufficient to establish the physical polarization at the sample. Stokes parameters inspect the actual complex vector. The sign convention for S3 and the time dependence are stated rather than silently assigning an LCP/RCP name.
blocks.check: For σ⁺=(1,i)/sqrt(2), S3 is +1 in this fixed laboratory basis; for a real nonzero linear state S3 is zero.

blocks.title: optical_state_audit — Trace incident and detection states back to the sample
blocks.explanation: At scan angles 0, 45 and 90 degrees, vector_samples evaluates Ein and effective_analyzer. Each column is passed to normalized_stokes. With ki=−Z and ks=+Z, the recorded propagation-relative expectations are −S3 for the incoming state and +S3 for the outgoing state. The returned record also retains B and both exact fields.
blocks.why: A linear analyzer after a return waveplate is generally an elliptical detection state when viewed at the sample. This audit prevents interpreting the analyzer hardware label as the sample polarization.
blocks.check: Compare the effective detection S3 values of QWP and CUBIC_SIGMA at intermediate angles; equal circular endpoints do not establish equal scans.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Prepare independent crystal-frame field samples
blocks.explanation: The audit transforms the actual input and effective detection vectors into crystal coordinates, evaluates every nonzero Cartesian tensor entry, adds the resulting amplitudes within each complete phonon tensor, and only then adds powers over orthogonal phonon components. Entry self-powers are stored separately. Their difference from the coherent result is the signed within-mode interference. A propagated roundoff bound protects exact dark channels without changing a curve. The audit caches incident and effective detector samples by optical profile. For a crystal, T*P.T embeds each transverse state in crystal coordinates; the 2D source uses its two-component fields directly.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-component handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Add entry amplitudes inside each complete tensor
blocks.explanation: For every orthogonal component, detection[row]* is multiplied by R[row,column] and incident[column]. The entry amplitudes are added before abs(amplitude)**2. Separately accumulated abs(entry)**2 terms provide the self-power diagnostic; coherent−self_power reveals all within-component cross terms.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-component handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Handle a dark-channel cancellation without altering intensity
blocks.explanation: The code estimates amplitude roundoff from uncancelled self-powers, propagates it into a power error bound, and combines it with a relative tolerance. This avoids dividing a cancellation residue by an almost-zero intensity. An actual mismatching coherent result raises ArithmeticError.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-component handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: tensor_interference_audit — Return complete audit arrays and their interpretation
blocks.explanation: The record retains the independently reconstructed coherent intensity, self-powers, signed interference, selected result, individual entry amplitudes, labels and error bounds. It explicitly says that component self-powers depend on the chosen basis, whereas the complete coherent result does not.
blocks.why: This deliberately uses entry-wise NumPy arithmetic instead of the production harmonic evaluator. Agreement is an independent check of rotation, conjugation, tensor-entry interference and phonon-component handling. An Ag entry split is an algebraic diagnostic, not three independent phonons.
blocks.check: Verify coherent_intensity = entry_self_power + interference. A tiny cancellation residue at a theoretical extinction may pass the roundoff bound, while an injected genuinely nonzero incorrect intensity must fail.

blocks.title: attach_physics_audit — Attach audit evidence without replacing results
blocks.explanation: For each optical profile, the function stores a sample-state audit. It calls tensor_interference_audit and records whether the selected calculation uses a coherent complete tensor or the explicit legacy component prescription. The run is returned with a new physics field; its calculated arrays remain untouched.
blocks.why: Diagnostics must explain or test a result rather than silently correcting it to a preferred plot. Separating audit data also makes exports reproducible.
blocks.check: The intensity arrays before and after this function should be equal; only additional physics metadata should appear.

blocks.title: physics_audit_markdown — Present polarization and interference checks
blocks.explanation: The reporter reads the audit record, displays the effective detection vector, and builds tables of polarization type and S3 at representative angles. It explains the laboratory-basis versus beam-direction convention and tabulates entry self-powers, interference, coherent intensity and the selected curve. Separate notes identify the source model and the legacy component prescription when applicable.
blocks.why: The reader needs to know what is being added as amplitudes and what is being added as powers. The tables make constructive and destructive interference visible and disclose the model scope.
blocks.check: A negative interference term is permitted, but the final measured-model intensity remains nonnegative. The reporter does not modify run["curves"].

blocks.explanation: The final print statement reports the code-cell number, the phrase “Run completed successfully.” and the functions or controls that are now ready. It is reached only if the preceding statements finish without an uncaught exception.
blocks.why: Definition cells otherwise run silently, which can be confusing for a new user. Execution status is separate from the scientific validation results in Cell 22.

pitfalls: The analyzer after a return waveplate is not generally the same Jones state as its linear transmission axis at the detector.
Same laboratory circular basis labels are not automatically same propagation-relative helicities in backscattering.
Tensor-entry self-powers are basis-dependent diagnostics; only the complete coherent intensity is invariant.
