blocks.title: Lattice and configuration checks
blocks.explanation: Check lattice lengths, angles and point-group constraints before constructing a frame.
blocks.why: Miller indices must be converted with the correct metric.
blocks.check: A cubic crystal must retain equal lattice lengths and 90° angles.

blocks.title: Compute amplitudes and sampled intensities
blocks.explanation: Build one amplitude record for each complete phonon tensor, then evaluate its squared modulus on the angular grid.
blocks.why: Entries within one phonon tensor add coherently; orthogonal unresolved phonon components add as powers.
blocks.check: The stored curves must agree with direct complex matrix contraction.

blocks.title: Create crystal inputs and display contributions
blocks.explanation: Create material values and separate Ag Cartesian contributions. Keep the complete mode in the audit record.

blocks.check: Do not add Ag component powers and call the result the complete coherent mode.

blocks.title: Three models and shared choices
blocks.explanation: Order the models New-san, My PPT slide, Dr. Kumar. Give each model VV, VH and σ⁺α and the same material list.
blocks.why: Changing a calculation presentation must not silently replace the physical inputs.
blocks.check: The controls must retain hkl, uvw, lattice, normal side, ψ and complex coefficients.

blocks.explanation: Validate inputs, build X/Y/Z and T, select Jones states and tensors, then run the common matrix engine. GaAs includes its LO/TO phonon projection.

blocks.check: Identical inputs give the same complete-mode intensity in the three routes.

overview: An independent symbolic reconstruction checks the special slide component prescription. It is deliberately outside the production curve engine.
workflow: Rotate real crystal unit vectors into the slide measurement frame.
Derive projected input/output overlap powers.
Expand each rank-one component intensity.
Recover the common denominator and regroup terms symbolically.
Apply the reference angles and compare only when the active reference conditions match.

blocks.title: Scope of this code section
blocks.explanation: A separate derivation/check of the user-provided component reference, not a plotting engine.
blocks.why: This module-level documentation identifies the responsibility of the following definitions and prevents confusing reference/report helpers with the active calculation engine.
blocks.check: Documentation does not execute a calculation or select coefficients.

blocks.title: component_ag_symbolics — Re-derive the slide component laws independently
blocks.explanation: The cached derivation rotates each rank-one diagonal component and builds its input/output overlap powers G(θ,β) and G(θ+α,β′). It expands the product, derives the common denominator from rational coefficients, collects a polynomial in the trigonometric factors, checks the regrouping identity and specializes θ=45 degrees and both phases to 90 degrees.
blocks.why: The regression must reconstruct the reference from geometry and Jones algebra. Deriving the denominator, rather than typing 144 into a final formula, makes the origin of the numerical factors auditable. This independent derivation is not called by the production curve engine.
blocks.check: The grouped and expanded polynomials must agree exactly. The individual specialized parts must reproduce the engine’s three slide-frame component curves.

blocks.title: component_reference_matches — Require exact reference conditions before showing its closed form
blocks.explanation: The function requires the legacy reference workflow, D2h Ag, the component-power rule, matching Jones parameters and the declared reference frame. It compares the actual frame numerically with the explicitly constructed reference frame.
blocks.why: A special-case expression must not be displayed as though it applies to an arbitrary material or orientation. This predicate prevents a reference equation being pasted into unrelated results.
blocks.check: A changed frame, changed detector phase or a GENERAL complete-mode calculation must return False, without modifying the input to make it pass.

blocks.title: component_ag_flow_markdown — Present the historical slide expansion only for a matching run
blocks.explanation: After the matching test, the reporter shows the input/output Jones vectors, each component law, the derived common denominator, the collected general expansion and its special-angle limit. It identifies the isolated intermediate θ−α transcription against the completed θ+α sequence and substitutes active coefficient magnitudes for the historical prescription.
blocks.why: The report preserves a reproducible legacy check while disclosing its component-power interpretation. Edition-14 main plots use separate component channels, so this legacy summed reporter is not their source.

blocks.explanation: Rz creates a rotation about z; inv is inversion; the diagonal matrices give twofold rotations or mirrors. c3, c4 and c6 set principal rotational generators, while cycle permutes the cubic Cartesian axes. The dictionary selects the required generators for each of the 21 groups.

blocks.title: Test complete symmetric tensor subspaces and irrep labels
blocks.explanation: Complex trial coefficients exercise all allowed entries. Each tensor must be symmetric and 3-by-3. Under every generator, transformed component tensors are expressed in the original component span using least squares; reconstruction and component-mixing unitarity are checked. Selected representation traces are compared with expected characters. Coefficient derivatives from all families must span the six-dimensional space of symmetric second-rank tensors.
blocks.why: Matrix shape alone cannot detect a mislabeled irrep, wrong off-diagonal sign or incomplete family. Covariance tests the transformation rule, while character traces distinguish representations.
blocks.check: The test reports its covariance and character counts. It validates the declared symmetric electric-dipole library, not arbitrary magnetic or nonsymmetric response tensors.

blocks.title: Reproduce the original QWP matrix chain independently
blocks.explanation: Check the explicit Q matrix, Q.H*Q=I, Q_return=Q.T and the circular incident state. For several complex source parameters, embed the effective 2D model only for regression and compare the engine curve with a closed circular-basis formula at irregular angles.

blocks.check: The 2D embedding in this test is an algebraic device; it is not a proposed symmetry tensor for CaNb2O6.

Compare the preserved historical component prescription and the coherent complete tensor against independent contractions, then change a relative phase to show their different interference rules. Invalid hybrid configurations must raise. Finally temporarily replace foreign crystal/reference helpers with functions that fail, run the pure source route and restore the globals in finally.

blocks.check: The preserved historical component-power sum is a regression target; the new main Ag figures remain separate xx/yy/zz contributions.

blocks.explanation: Use a reproducible complex random tensor on three surfaces with a noncubic metric and nonzero frame angle. For three optical chains and five angles, NumPy contracts the embedded incident/detection vectors with the full rotated tensor independently of the reduced calculation. Also test det(T)=+1 and invariance of an isotropic tensor.
